the_contrast_that_defines_this_session.explanation: the 60% figure came from tasks selected BECAUSE earlier policies failed them and then repaired until they passed. The unselected number is the honest one.

failure_taxonomy_at_scale.never_attempted_no_procedure: 28 of 40 in the random sample; 46 of 60 in the walk sample
failure_taxonomy_at_scale.why: the policy has five goal-shape procedures (Enter "X", slider value, A>B>C menu, native select, drag-box). MiniWob's remaining families ask for arithmetic, counting, reading tables, drawing, resizing, hot-cold search, simon-says recall, and more. Each needs a different procedure and none is derivable from the five.
failure_taxonomy_at_scale.attempted_but_failed: 7 of 12 attempted: click-menu (menu-miss), use-autocomplete x2, drag-cube, form-sequence-3, social-media, click-dialog

established: one demonstration produces a permanent, transferring procedure (2/6 -> 8/8 same task; 9/10 different task)
relation-type procedures transfer across widget families (drag 6/6 first try)
calibration failures are repaired by closed loop then completed by raising actuator resolution (slider 0/6 -> 2/5 -> 10/10)
the learning machinery (universal_learning_contract_v1) is fail-closed and passes 153 tests
GUI fault localisation from repeated execution works (ochiai 1.0, both statistics agreeing)
NOT_established: any claim that computer use is substantially solved: the unselected reach is 10-12.5%
that more learning would raise that number: it would not, because 70% of tasks are never attempted
the GDPval elo target, unreachable from this sandbox

the_first_principles_position: reach = (fraction of tasks the agent has a procedure for) x (success rate when it has one). This session maximised the second factor (it is 5/12 and one-demonstration-learnable) and left the first at 30%. The first factor is a COVERAGE question and it is answered by decomposing unfamiliar goal sentences into primitive operations, not by storing more skills and not by learning faster.
the_sentience_question_answered_directly: no. The system stores rules, gates them behind a verifier, and acts only on instructions it is given. Delete the store and the rules are gone; there is no unobserved persistent state and no endogenous goal. It is a governed library, not a creature.
